name: Ball Carrier
description: Possession as a physical state: who has the ball, what it costs them, and how it leaves. Carrying constrains the carrier — a speed multiplier, no tackling while holding — because possession must cost something or every player on the pitch is always the ball. Passing and shooting hand the ball to movement.physics_core as a free body with intent metadata (target teammate, lead distance); a ball in flight belongs to physics, and possession is only re-adjudicated on contact, never claimed at range. Dribbling is a leash, not a weld: the ball stays within controlRadius while control holds, and hard direction changes test controlRating to see whether it comes loose — which is what makes movement.skill_move_set's committed moves a gamble instead of a combo video.

inputs.name: controlRadius
inputs.description: Leash distance between carrier and ball while dribbling. Wide enough that sprinting doesn't outrun the ball, tight enough that defenders can see the gap they are aiming a tackle at.

inputs.name: carrierSpeedMultiplier
inputs.description: Movement speed scale while in possession. The tax that makes off-ball runs matter — if the carrier is fastest, the correct play is never to pass, and the sport collapses into a relay.

inputs.name: passSpeed
inputs.description: Launch speed of a pass toward its target, with lead distance computed from the target's velocity. A pass is a prediction; the metadata rides with the ball so interceptions can be credited to the reader, not the roller.

inputs.name: shotSpeed
inputs.description: Launch speed of a shot. Faster than any pass because a shot is the one ball nobody is expected to catch — world.goal_zone and the keeper both read the same incoming physics body.

inputs.name: controlRating
inputs.description: 0-1 chance the leash holds through a hard direction change or contact. This is the per-player skill knob; movement.skill_move_set borrows it for its success rolls rather than keeping a second dribble stat.

outputs.name: hasPossession
outputs.description: True while this entity holds the ball. Exactly one entity in the match should report true at any tick; the component treats duplicate possession as a bug, not a shared-custody feature.

outputs.name: ballState
outputs.description: carried, inFlight, or loose. Everything downstream — referee context, AI positioning, the goal zone — reads this one word instead of reconstructing it from positions.
